newsitem.title: IRAQ: France's Elf, Iraq dicuss oil sale, exploration.
newsitem.headline: France's Elf, Iraq dicuss oil sale, exploration.

text.p: The French energy group Elf Aquitaine has submitted an offer to Iraq to buy oil once the United Nations gives the green light under an oil-for-food deal, the Elf representative in Baghdad said on Monday.
"We have already...put our own offer to buy Iraq's oil and sell to Iraq medicine produced by our company," Elf representative Yves J. Serre told Reuters.

He said that Elf was conducting talks with the Iraqi government on extracting oil from the Majnoon field in southern Iraq. The field could produce at least 300,000 barrels per day (bpd) when developed.
"We are having talks with the (Iraqi) Oil Ministry definitely. They started some time ago and are still continuing.
"When the sanctions are lifted we will try our best to get and implement the contract," he said.

The sanctions, imposed by the United Nations on Iraq for its 1990 invasion of Kuwait, prevent Baghdad from exporting its oil and importing goods except for food and medicine, for which it has little cash.
Under a deal signed with the United Nations on May 20, Iraq is allowed to sell $2 billion worth of oil in six months on a renewable basis to raise money to buy urgent needs.
The deal was suspended when Baghdad sent troops into northern Iraq in August to help one Kurdish faction against a rival.

A representative from another French oil company, Total SA, is also in Baghdad. The government daily al-Jumhouriya said on Sunday Total was holding talks with Iraqi officials, trying to conclude a deal to develop oilfields.
Total is aiming to develop the giant Nahr Umar field in the south whose production capacity is around 500,000 bpd.
Elf and Total have been negotiating with Iraq since 1992 about developing Iraqi oilfields once the embargo is lifted.
Iraq has said that in awarding business contracts it will favour countries which stood by it during the sanctions.
France, Russia and China, are pressing for a partial lifting of the sanctions.
China said on Monday that it was holding talks with Iraq on the possibility of signing oil exploration contracts.
Russian Foreign Minister Yevgeny Primakov, after meeting Iraqi deputy Prime Minister Tareq Aziz in Moscow on Sunday, called for the Security Council to implement the oil-for-food deal.
